edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Apollinem facitis citharaedum atque divinum. Primum de Maia natus in insula Delo, Oblata mercede postmodum structor, obsecutus Laomedonti regi Trojanorum muros eduxit. Locavitque sese, quem deum seducti putatis: Ossibus cujus amor Cassandrae flagravit, Subdole quem lusit virgo, falliturque divinus. Officio vervecis potuit scire bicordem. Repudiatus enim discessit inde divinus. Terruit hunc virgo specie, quam ille deberet. Illa prior quae debuerat deum amavisse, Lasciviens qui Daphnem sic coepit amare: Et tamen insequitur, dum vult violare puellam; Gratis amat stultus, nec potuit consequi cursu. Vel, si deus erat, occurreret illi per auras. Sub tectis illa prior venit, remansit que divinus. Fallit vos gens hominum, nam victu tristi fuerunt. Admeti pecora quoque pavisse refertur. Lusibus impositis dum mitteret discum in altum, Sublapsum non potuit retinere: prostravit amicum: Ultimus ille dies fuit Hyacinthi sodalis. Si divinus erat, mortem praescisset amici.
pass_a_gloss: You make Apollo a cithara player and divine. First born from Maia on the island Delos, afterwards with a wage offered he followed as a builder, and having followed King Laomedon of the Trojans he built walls. And he settled himself, whom as a god deceived people think: with bones of whom love for Cassandra blazed, subtly whom the virgin deceived and the divine one is deceived. By the office of a shepherd he was able to know the two-hearted one. For the divine one having been rejected departed from there. The virgin terrified him with appearance, which he ought to have. She who first ought to have loved the god, who began to love Daphne lustfully: and yet he pursues, while he wants to violate the girl; the foolish one loves gratuitously and he was not able to attain by pursuit. Or if he was a god, he would have met her through the air. The virgin came first under the roof and the divine one remained. The human race deceives you, for they were with sad food. Also it is reported that he pastured the flocks of Admetus. With games imposed while he was sending the discus into the air, the one having slipped he was not able to retain: he knocked down the friend: that was the last day of Hyacinth the comrade. If he was divine, he would have foreknown the death of the friend.

choices.why: participle indicating the state of being deceived
substantive participle used as a noun

pass_b_english: You make Apollo a cithara player and divine. First born from Maia on the island of Delos, afterwards he followed King Laomedon of the Trojans as a builder for a wage offered, and built walls. And he settled himself, whom you, deceived, think is a god: in whose bones love for Cassandra blazed, whom the virgin deceived subtly, and the divine one is deceived. By the office of a shepherd he was able to know the two-hearted one. For the divine one, having been rejected, departed from there. The virgin terrified him with an appearance which he ought to have had. She who first ought to have loved the god, who began to love Daphne lustfully: and yet he pursues, while he wants to violate the girl; the foolish one loves gratuitously and he was not able to overtake her by pursuit. Or if he was a god, he would have met her through the air. The virgin came first under the roof and the divine one remained. The human race deceives you, for they lived with sad food. Also it is reported that he pastured the flocks of Admetus. With games imposed while he was sending the discus into the air, the one that had slipped he was not able to retain: he knocked down the friend: that was the last day of Hyacinth the comrade. If he was divine, he would have foreknown the death of the friend.
